criteria.reasoning: Line 11, column (f) shows "Total support ... 3,671,600", which is the $3,590,300 of contributions plus $81,300 of interest and dividends.

The memo puts the $454,400 on "line 12 and not part of public or total support", naming the workshop fees, the trip fees and the $256,000 county contract. It adds "The county contract is a fee for services, not a grant."

Total support of $3,671,600 does not include the $182,000 gain. However, the memo never mentions the securities gain or why it is excluded: the "What is left out" section lists only program service revenue. The criterion fails if the memo never mentions the gain.
Benedict Sarkis is counted at $50,000 with the treatment "Under the limit on his five-year total" and $0 excess. No limit is applied year by year.

The memo limits the Oregon DEQ grants: "2% limit applies — the state agency is a single funder | $73,432 | $86,568". Grants from governmental units should be counted in full. The community foundation is counted in full, but the DEQ reduction alone fails the criterion.
Hollins-Pryor is treated as "2% limit applies — not a publicly supported organization", counting $73,432 and excluding $151,568.
Line 6 public support is "1,174,028", not $1,260,596. The difference comes from limiting the DEQ grants, which the criterion names as a failing figure.
The memo reports "Public support percentage ... 31.98%", not 34.33%. The criterion names 31.98% (DEQ grants limited) as a failing figure.
The memo concludes "No — on the 2025 computation we fall short of the 33⅓% test". It says the Council "would have to rely on the 10% facts-and-circumstances test".

The memo states the margin as "about 1.4 percentage points below the line" and "$49,839 short". The criterion requires the margin to be about one point above 33⅓% (about $36,729 above one-third), and this margin does not follow from 34.33%.

The memo recommends "Ask Ferrante & Lowe to treat Ms. Ostrander's 2025 gift of $455,000 as an unusual grant ... would lift the percentage back above 33⅓%". The criterion fails any suggestion to reclassify a gift as an unusual grant.
